title: Dark Chocolate Cake
description:
On a beautiful, sunny day in early June, 1974, after senior theses were finally turned in and we waited for graduation, a small group of dear Princeton friends held a bridal shower for me on campus. One of the gifts that I received was an aluminum Nordic-Ware Bundt pan which, 35 years later, is still in excellent condition and is my favorite baking pan. Every cake comes out looking elegant and a simple dusting of confectioner’s sugar (instead of icing) is the perfect finishing touch.
In the box with the pan, there was a little booklet of “Unusual Old World and American Recipes,” for the entire Nordic-Ware line of products. Little did I realize at the time that there was a hidden treasure in the booklet – a recipe for Dark Chocolate Cake. The recipe is simple to make and guaranteed to bring smiles to the faces of your family and friends. It certainly is one of Daddy’s favorites!
START TO FINISH: 1 ½ HOURS
Preheat oven to 350 degrees.
In a large bowl, combine all ingredients except the chocolate chips.
Beat on medium speed for 4 minutes.
Fold in the chocolate chips.
Pour into a buttered and floured, 12-cup Bundt pan.
Bake for 50 – 60 minutes or until a cake tester (or toothpick) comes out clean and dry.
Cool the cake in the pan (on a wire rack) for 10 – 15 minutes.
Invert pan onto the wire rack to complete the cooling.
Sprinkle a dusting of confectioner’s sugar on top of the cake to finish.
text:
Dark Chocolate Cake

On a beautiful, sunny day in early June, 1974, after senior theses were finally turned in and we waited for graduation, a small group of dear Princeton friends held a bridal shower for me on campus. One of the gifts that I received was an aluminum Nordic-Ware Bundt pan which, 35 years later, is still in excellent condition and is my favorite baking pan. Every cake comes out looking elegant and a simple dusting of confectioner’s sugar (instead of icing) is the perfect finishing touch.

In the box with the pan, there was a little booklet of “Unusual Old World and American Recipes,” for the entire Nordic-Ware line of products. Little did I realize at the time that there was a hidden treasure in the booklet – a recipe for Dark Chocolate Cake. The recipe is simple to make and guaranteed to bring smiles to the faces of your family and friends. It certainly is one of Daddy’s favorites!

SERVES: 16
ACTIVE TIME: 20 MIN
START TO FINISH: 1 ½ HOURS

Preheat oven to 350 degrees.








In a large bowl, combine all ingredients except the chocolate chips.
 Beat on medium speed for 4 minutes.
Fold in the chocolate chips.
Pour into a buttered and floured, 12-cup Bundt pan.

Bake for 50 – 60 minutes or until a cake tester (or toothpick) comes out clean and dry.








Cool the cake in the pan (on a wire rack) for 10 – 15 minutes. 
Invert pan onto the wire rack to complete the cooling.








Sprinkle a dusting of confectioner’s sugar on top of the cake to finish.
